concept: AppShell is the case that holds a whole screen of an appliance app: the header unit across the top, the page legend down the side, the main window beside it and a footer unit under it, each its own unit with a gap between. On a narrow window the legend folds away into a flap that slides in from the side.

default_to_avoid.pattern: app shell with a full-bleed top bar, a flush sidebar and a content area divided by hard rules (admin dashboard frame)
default_to_avoid.why_not: Regions glued to the window edge and split by dark rules read as one wall; dial keeps each region a unit with an inset gap and never separates regions of one screen by a hard rule.

default_to_avoid.pattern: AppShell as a second Container that only centres content
default_to_avoid.why_not: Container only sets a reading width and has no landmarks; the AppShell places header, side navigation, main and footer, folds the side column into a Drawer and moves focus on a route change.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the dial, the band list and the case set as separate fields on one face, each with its own margin
Vitsoe 606 Universal Shelving (Dieter Rams, 1960): separate units on a fixed module, none touching the wall by its own edge
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Landmark Regions and the skip-link technique: banner, navigation, main and contentinfo, and a first link that jumps to main

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The header, the side column, main and footer keep their places on one grid; opening and closing the menu, or collapsing the Sidebar, never moves main out of its row.

derivation.consequence: capped so large panels do not swell into pillows
derivation.form: The shell is not a body of its own. It sets the inset gap between the units it holds, and each unit keeps its own capped panel radius.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: Header, side column, main and footer all start on the same inset line at the inline start and stop at the same one at the inline end.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: A skip link is the first stop and moves focus to main; a route change moves focus to main again; below the breakpoint the side column opens in a Drawer from the Menu key.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The shell paints nothing orange; the one primary key of the screen belongs to the unit that holds it, and the shell's own Menu key is plain.

options.name: four separate units on the page ground with gaps between
one case split into regions by hairlines
side column at full height with the header only over main

variants.reason: A follows the separator rule (gaps first, never a hard rule between regions) and keeps the header across the whole top so it stays the banner; B cuts one body with rules, which FORM forbids, and C breaks the header into a title bar that no longer holds the brand.

root.why: A grid on the page ground with the inset gap on all four sides and between regions, so the units never touch the window or each other.

body.why: The row between header and footer holds the side column and main on one grid, and it takes the height left so the footer stays at the foot.

header.why: The header slot spans the full width on the top inset line, and it can hold at the top edge while the page scrolls.

side.why: The side column keeps the width of its Sidebar at the inline start of the second row, so the legend stays in one fixed column.

main.why: Main takes all the width the side column leaves and is the target of the skip link and of focus on a route change.

footer.why: The optional footer spans the full width on the bottom inset line, like printing at the foot of a case.

trigger.why: Below the breakpoint, and when no header takes the Menu key, a plain 44px key opens the side column in a Drawer.

data-layout=single.why: With no side column, or one folded into a Drawer, the grid drops to a single column and main keeps its row.

data-sticky.why: A held header stays at the top inset line while the page scrolls under it, on the page ground so nothing shows through the gap.

focus-visible.why: Main takes focus from the skip link or a route change, so it draws the same ring as every part when the keyboard put it there.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the ring on main uses the system highlight colour, because author colours are replaced.
